content_units: Best Laptop Pick for an Engineering Student
With your priorities in order—  battery life  ,   16GB RAM minimum  , and   good Linux compatibility   under   $1,100  —the   Lenovo ThinkPad E14 Gen 5   is the best overall fit.
Why it wins:
-   Best Linux track record   of the three thanks to the ThinkPad line’s long-standing Linux friendliness
-   Largest battery   here at   57Wh
-   Portable   at   1.41kg
- Strong CPU for coding, CAD-lite workloads, MATLAB, Python, simulations, and multitasking
- Stays well under budget at   $949
Ranked Comparison Table
Rank   Laptop   Price   Battery / Portability   Linux Compatibility   Key Tradeoff
1     Lenovo ThinkPad E14 Gen 5       $949       57Wh  , 1.41kg, 14" 1920x1200     Best     SSD is 512GB, not 1TB
2     HP Pavilion Plus 14       $1,049     51Wh, 1.40kg, 14" 2240x1400 OLED   Good but less predictable than ThinkPad   OLED display may reduce battery life
3     ASUS Vivobook 15       $899     50Wh, 1.70kg, 15.6" 1920x1080   Usually workable, but less consistent   Heavier and likely weaker real-world battery life
Why This Ranking Fits Your Priorities
1) Lenovo ThinkPad E14 Gen 5 — Best overall
Option 1:   Lenovo ThinkPad E14 Gen 5     Best balance of battery life, Linux support, portability, and performance     Top recommendation
Search model
-   Battery life:   Best on paper because it has the   largest battery   and a power-efficient   Ryzen 7 7730U
-   Linux compatibility:   This is the strongest point.   ThinkPads are widely used with Linux  , and driver/support issues are typically fewer than on mainstream consumer laptops
-   Engineering use:   16GB RAM is enough for typical student workloads: CAD entry-level work, programming, VMs, circuit tools, MATLAB, IDEs, browser tabs
-   Display:   14-inch   1920x1200   gives a little more vertical space than 1080p, which helps for coding and documents
-   Value:   At   $949  , it gives you strong specs without stretching the budget
Best for:
- Students planning to run   Ubuntu, Fedora, Pop! OS, or dual-boot Linux
- Daily campus carry
- Long library/classroom use away from outlets
2) HP Pavilion Plus 14 — Best screen, good performance, weaker battery certainty
Option 2:   HP Pavilion Plus 14     Premium screen and modern Ryzen chip, but battery is less dependable for your top priority     Best alternative
Search model
-   Performance:   Ryzen 5 7640U is a very capable modern chip and should feel fast for student workloads
-   Display:   The   2240x1400 OLED   is easily the nicest screen of the three
-   Portability:   Very close to the Lenovo at   1.40kg
-   Linux compatibility:   Often fine, but   not as safe a bet as a ThinkPad
-   Battery tradeoff:   OLED panels usually look great but can   consume more power  , especially with bright backgrounds common in coding, note-taking, and web use
Best for:
- Students who care a lot about   display quality
- Users who will spend more time plugged in
- Those okay with a bit more Linux uncertainty than Lenovo
3) ASUS Vivobook 15 — Best storage value, but lowest fit for your priorities
Option 3:   ASUS Vivobook 15     Good price and 1TB storage, but weaker match for battery life and Linux-first use     Budget/value option
Search model
-   Best storage:     1TB SSD   is generous for class files, CAD files, projects, and dual-boot setups
-   Price:   Cheapest at   $899
-   Battery outlook:   Despite an efficient i7-1355U, the   50Wh battery   plus   larger 15.6-inch display   and heavier chassis usually hurt mobility
-   Portability:   At   1.70kg  , it’s noticeably less convenient for daily campus carry
-   Linux compatibility:   Often usable, but consumer ASUS models can be   less predictable   for suspend, function keys, audio quirks, and firmware polish than ThinkPads
Best for:
- Students who want the   lowest upfront cost
- Users who prioritize   storage   over battery and Linux reliability
- More desk-based than backpack-based use
Decision Notes for Your Use Case
Best choice: Lenovo ThinkPad E14 Gen 5
It is the most aligned with your stated priorities in order:
-   Battery life:   strongest spec here
-   16GB RAM minimum:   yes
-   Linux compatibility:   strongest reputation by a clear margin
Trade-off alternative: HP Pavilion Plus 14
Choose this only if:
- You value the   display   enough to accept likely shorter battery life
- Linux compatibility is important, but not your absolute top concern after battery
Value alternative: ASUS Vivobook 15
Choose this only if:
- You want to save money and get   1TB storage
- You are okay with a heavier laptop and potentially less polished Linux behavior
